hints: Use the binomial expansion of $(1+4x)^{1/2}$ far enough to identify its $x^2$ and $x^3$ coefficients.
The required $x^3$ term in $(3+x)(1+4x)^{1/2}$ comes from $3$ times the $x^3$ term and $x$ times the $x^2$ term.
Add those two contributions to obtain the requested coefficient.
walkthrough:
Write the square root in index form:
$$\sqrt{1 + 4x} = (1 + 4x)^{1/2}$$

State the general binomial expansion for $(1 + y)^n$ where $n = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $y = 4x$:
$$(1 + y)^{1/2} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}y + \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{2!}y^2 + \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{3!}y^3 + \dots$$

Calculate the coefficient of $x^2$ in the expansion of $(1 + 4x)^{1/2}$:
$$\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{2}(4x)^2 = -\dfrac{1}{8}(16x^2) = -2x^2$$

Calculate the coefficient of $x^3$ in the expansion of $(1 + 4x)^{1/2}$:
$$\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{6}(4x)^3 = \dfrac{\frac{3}{8}}{6}(64x^3) = \dfrac{1}{16}(64x^3) = 4x^3$$

Expand $(3 + x)(1 + 4x)^{1/2}$ to collect all terms of degree 3 in $x$:
$$(3 + x)(1 + \dots - 2x^2 + 4x^3 + \dots)$$
$$\text{Term from } 3 \times (4x^3) = 12x^3$$
$$\text{Term from } x \times (-2x^2) = -2x^3$$

Sum the terms to find the total coefficient of $x^3$:
$$12x^3 - 2x^3 = 10x^3$$
$$\text{Coefficient of } x^3 = 10$$
